changes: Name normalized to a-stem 'Manateja': the cataloguer's emendation manateja(sya) is a genitive in -sya, which points to the stem Manateja. Manatejas would give Manatejasaḥ.
Confidence lowered from high to medium: the form is corrupt, and the genitive after liṣiti could also mark ownership, though scribe is the usual reading.
Tithi normalized to pratipadā (1); the form as written is kept in the notes.
Note added that the era is only 'samvat'. Nepāla Saṃvat is inferred from the Newari script and the low number.

notes: The era is written only as 'samvat'. NS (564 + 880 = 1444 CE) is inferred from the Newari script and the low year number. The tithi is written 'pradīpa(dyā)', a corruption of pratipadā. 'liṣiti' stands for likhitam. The name is written manatejaḥ and the cataloguer emends it to manatejasya, so it is read here as the a-stem Manateja. A genitive after likhitam normally names the scribe, but it could also be read as 'written for/belonging to' Manateja. 'saptasaptyā' in the title is a corruption of saptaśatyā.
